title: Term existence / obsoletion
explanation: Provenance of origin: the external class a term was copied/cloned from, with date (D-030); today not recorded (kBOOM 'MONDO:Leader' marker was deleted in 2018; recoverable for ~57% of terms). Request/discussion: GitHub term tracker items (provenance, D-036). Curator (ORCID, D-004). Obsolescence reason and replacement on obsolete terms. Corroborating external records are evidence, not origin.

title: Definition
explanation: Definition dbxrefs mean 'inspired by' (provenance, not verbatim, not confirmation) (D-031). Curator ORCID when edited. Design-pattern origin derived at build time by matching against pattern files, not stored (D-020). Definition without any source on a live term: allowed, validation warning, curation backlog (D-029).

title: Synonym (exact, related, narrow, broad)
explanation: Synonym dbxrefs (all scopes) mean 'currently supported by' (evidence), time-sensitive: support lapses if the source drops the name, so a date/source version is needed (D-031). Community endorsement (OMO:0002001) recorded as an endorsing agent (D-034, provisional). Pattern-generated synonyms get derived pattern provenance (D-020).

title: Subclass placement
explanation: External records asserting the same subclass are concordance evidence (D-004); origin separately (D-030). Curator ORCID. Supporting documents (PMID) are evidence (D-037). Source-level attribution without a record ID allowed (MONDO:DOID etc., D-025). Reasoning status (redundant/entailed) is computed, not stored; evidence must be attachable to entailed axioms (D-018).

title: Negative subclass (excluded subclass)
explanation: A claim in its own right with negative polarity (D-032). The curator (ORCID, ~99% coverage) asserts it. External records on it assert the positive subclass and are recorded as evidence DISPUTING Mondo's claim (D-033): requires evidence direction.

title: Mapping (cross-reference)
explanation: Predicate comes from the Mondo precision code, not evidence (D-006, D-008, D-014). Obsolete-side markers (D-009, D-010), obsolete-to-obsolete = warning state (D-011), preferredExternal with direction-dependent semantics (D-012), OMIM included entries as value-set relation (D-013). Uncoded xrefs: provider authority for GARD/NORD/NANDO, warning otherwise (D-017). Provider (MedGen, EFO, NANDO, MalaCards) vs asserter (GARD, NORD) roles (D-002). Review state incl. 'not verified' (D-024).

title: Disease attribute (definitional)
explanation: Supporting evidence: documents (PMID, D-037), external records (OMIM, Orphanet). Asserters include ClinGen expert panels (affiliation URL, D-002) and curators (ORCID).

title: Subset membership
explanation: Asserted by a provider (GARD, NORD, Orphanet) or declared by a stakeholder (Open Targets 'otar', ClinGen) (D-002). Status-flag subsets (obsoletion_candidate, speculative, ...) are term metadata outside EPC (D-035).

title: Metaclass / kind of class (CANDIDATE)
explanation: Needs its own evidence (e.g. a source's own typing such as Orphanet disorder/group/subtype) and an asserting curator. Current subsets drift (30 classes tagged both grouping and Orphanet disorder; mondo#685).

title: Value-set membership (CANDIDATE)
explanation: Separate from mapping relationships (D-013, D-040). Today encoded as xref + MONDO:includedEntryInOMIM, exported as skos:relatedMatch (interim).

title: Direct Slot–Value on a Parent Record
explanation: Current: every Mondo claim is a slot/value on the term stanza in mondo-edit.obo (is_a, xref, synonym, relationship, ...). Desired: kept as the plain consumption form (e.g. term-centric OBO/JSON without provenance) alongside the nested form below (D-041). All claim types C001-C010.

title: Nested Structured Claim Object within Parent Record
explanation: Current: axiom annotations on each slot line ({source=...}) act as a lightweight nested object inside the term record. Desired: the PRIMARY authoring form AND a consumption form: one term-centric record per disease with nested statement objects carrying curator, evidence (with direction and dates), origin provenance and review state (view 'A', D-041). Many users want term-centric records for consumption, so this structure must be preserved, not only transformed away.

title: Reified Claim / Statement Object
explanation: Current: no first-class, identified statement objects (OWL axiom annotations are anonymous reification). Desired: GENERATED from the term-centric form as the SEPIO exchange view ('B', D-041): stable statement IDs, so evidence can attach to entailed axioms (D-018), negative claims (D-032), review state (D-024). The term-centric form must carry everything needed to generate it.

title: Direct Edge / Triple in a Graph
explanation: Current: releases (OWL, SKOS via mk-skos.pl, SSSOM, KGX downstream) emit direct edges with provenance mostly flattened away. Desired: kept as the release view ('C', D-041); may carry edge-level provenance where formats allow.

title: Other
explanation: n/a

title: Human-Readable Claim Text
explanation: Mondo terms have labels, but statements have no text of their own. mondo-ai evidence packets generate statement_text (e.g. "peripartum cardiomyopathy has exact synonym 'postpartum peripartum cardiomyopathy'") for human review: useful, not required.

title: SPO Semantics on Statement
explanation: The generated statement objects (D-041 view B) carry subject, predicate and object directly, as mondo-ai's SIEVE SieveStatement already does. The Mondo edit file stays term-centric; the statement model coexists with it via a LinkML-Map transformation (D-042).

title: SPO Semantics in Nested Proposition
explanation: Not needed. Concordance (an external source asserting the same axiom, D-004) and disputing evidence (D-033) are established by matching subject/predicate/object plus a negation flag, not by shared proposition objects.

title: Qualifying / Contextual Information
explanation: Mapping qualifiers: object obsolete in source version V (D-010), preferred among 1:n exact matches and direction of validity (D-012), value-set membership (D-013, C010). Negative polarity for excluded subclass (D-032). Today partly encoded as MONDO: codes in the source slot.

title: Directly Corresponding Prior Claim — Text Passage
Directly Corresponding Prior Claim — Structured Data
Evidence Interpretation Requirement
explanation: Core requirement for Mondo (D-044). Interpretation happens at two levels: evidence lines (per evidence, support/dispute with strength) and an overall assertion decision on top (D-045). The act of interpreting must be represented: who (human with perspective, or AI with its failure modes), how, on which evidence. Mondo itself only holds human-curated evidence; one evidence model is shared with mondo-ai.

title: Evidence Interpretation Direction
explanation: Supports / disputes. First Mondo use case: external sources asserting a subclass that Mondo negates (excluded_subClassOf) are disputing evidence (D-033). Human dissent is a disputing line (D-051).

title: Evidence Interpretation Strength (categorical)
explanation: Human-readable label, possibly derived from numeric score bands (D-047). Per claim type (e.g. ClinGen-style definitive / strong / moderate / limited for gene-disease, D-054).

title: Evidence Interpretation Strength (numeric)
explanation: PRIMARY: the numeric score drives the curation queue (D-047). Each claim type has its own versioned aggregation rule (D-054), all normalised onto a shared 0-1 scale so scores are comparable across claims. The axiom-level score is computed by the rule and a human signs off (D-048). Weighted by who produced each line: human signers by role/expertise level, AI agents by trust (D-049, D-052).

title: Evidence Line Granularity
explanation: PARKED (D-046): whether an evidence line interprets exactly one item or can group items. Trade-off: one item per line is simple and checkable but over-counts correlated evidence; grouping captures the argument but needs criteria.

title: Evidence Item Grouping Criteria
explanation: Depends on the parked granularity decision. Independently of it, dependence MUST be representable: sources derived from sources (DOID from OMIM; EFO imports Mondo), several publications on the same study, and one collective decision with many participants (D-046).

title: Contradictory Evidence
explanation: Claims can be kept despite disputing evidence (assertion outcome 'controversial', D-053). Disputing lines enter the per-claim-type rule (D-054). Rejected claims are kept on record with their evidence (D-053). Competing interpretations count too: a claim that cannot be true together with the scored one (the same exact synonym on another disease, or the same pair under another relation) enters as one 'competing claim' refuting line, weight ln(1 + sum of e^L over competitors, from their own evidence); exclusivity is defined per claim type, and contested claims are never auto-accepted (D-069).

title: Evidence Line Stacking
explanation: Possible route for grouped arguments (higher-order lines over item lines) if the parked granularity question (D-046) is resolved that way.

title: Distinct Evidence Models
explanation: Yes: one versioned aggregation rule per claim type (synonym, gene-disease, mapping, ...), normalised to a shared 0-1 scale (D-054). Candidate rule sources: ClinGen gene-disease validity SOP (C007), mondo-ai maprule (C006).

title: Evidence Line-Item Collapsing
explanation: No. Evidence lines are explicit, immutable objects, separate from evidence items (D-045, D-052). Lines are invalidated (excluded from the score), never edited or deleted; corrections are new lines.

title: Direct Evidence Item Linking
explanation: Today every Mondo source annotation is a direct axiom-to-item link with no interpretation. Retained for lightweight consumption (term-centric view, D-041), but desired data also carries evidence lines.

title: Source-only Evidence Citation
explanation: Source-level attribution without a record ID is kept (MONDO:DOID, MONDO:OMIM, ...; D-025). PMIDs cited without the specific passage are also source-only citations (D-037).

title: Evidence Item Provenance: Agent
explanation: Current: implicit only, via the CURIE prefix. Desired: the resource a cited term belongs to is explicit, at resource (organisation) level, via a resource registry (e.g. the information-resource registry used in OMO:0002001). Individual upstream curators or authors are not recorded (D-055).

title: Evidence Item Provenance: Method Types
explanation: Upstream evidence only; for evidence records created in the Mondo ecosystem (snippets) the method IS recorded (D-057). PROVISIONAL, to revisit (D-056). How upstream evidence was produced is the upstream resource's business. Where the kind of evidence matters for strength (e.g. functional study vs case report for gene-disease), it enters through the per-claim-type aggregation rule (D-054), not as provenance Mondo maintains.

title: Evidence Item Provenance: Specific Methods / Specifications
explanation: Upstream evidence only; for created evidence records see D-057. PROVISIONAL, to revisit together with PROV.EI.METHOD_TYPES (D-056).

title: Evidence Item Provenance: Resources
explanation: Upstream evidence only; for created evidence records see D-057. PROVISIONAL, may be revised (D-056). Upstream detail. The species of non-human disease evidence is already a Mondo claim of its own (in_taxon, C007), not evidence provenance.

title: Evidence Item Provenance: Execution Details
explanation: Upstream evidence (the paper, the OMIM record): N. Evidence records CREATED in the Mondo ecosystem (text snippets extracted from papers, structured statements pulled from records): Y, with full creation provenance: who (human or AI agent, model/workflow version), when, from which document and version, exact location, extraction method, and verification outcome (D-057, D-050). The same applies to the other PROV.EI rows for created records. Read coverage (abstract only vs full text) and access status (paywalled) are mandatory for document-based interpretations (D-059).

title: Evidence Item Provenance: Date
explanation: Y for upstream evidence (when the evidence was produced: paper publication date, record creation/revision date): highly valuable, since recency can inform the per-claim-type rules (D-054). Sourced via the preprocessed, versioned source snapshots, which must carry it (D-058). Y for evidence records created in the Mondo ecosystem (D-057). Distinct from when Mondo read the upstream item (D-055, PROV.EI.RETRIEVAL_SOURCE).

title: Evidence Item Provenance: Context / Location
explanation: Not needed: collapses into PROV.EI.AGENT for Mondo. Mondo holds no experimental evidence, so physical conditions never apply; records Mondo creates are located by run identifier and workflow version (D-050 #1).

title: Evidence Item Provenance: Retrieval Source
explanation: The resource a cited term belongs to (explicit), when it was read, and the source version (D-055). Must be carried in the preprocessed source snapshots (D-058). Today only the identifier is stored.

title: Evidence Item Provenance: Quality
explanation: Inherent quality of the evidence itself, at two levels: per resource (maintained once in a resource registry) and per item (e.g. retraction, case report vs cohort study). Feeds the per-claim-type aggregation rules (D-054) alongside agent trust (D-049, D-052) and read coverage (D-059). Levels must be dated so re-rating does not rewrite past scores (D-060).

title: Evidence Item Provenance: Evidence Generation Context
explanation: Y for publications (study / publication type, e.g. PubMed publication types) AND for prior claims inside external records where the source exposes their evidential basis (e.g. Orphanet gene-disease association validation status and supporting PMIDs, OMIM phenotype mapping keys). Today an n=1 association and a large study in Orphanet look identical in Mondo ({source="Orphanet:..."}). Where the basis is not exposed it is recorded as unknown, not assumed strong. Feeds the per-claim-type rules (D-054); metadata via source snapshots (D-058).

title: Semantic Alignment Provenance: Agent
explanation: Y for automated and AI alignment (agent identity incl. model/workflow version, D-050 #1). N for human curators: their alignment is an implicit cognitive step, covered by the human interpretation and assertion acts (D-051). Scope: all three alignment kinds: text -> structure (snippets), term -> term (mappings), source ingest (D-061).

title: Semantic Alignment Provenance: Method Types
explanation: PROVISIONAL: proposal to adopt the MeDIC transformation-provenance vocabulary (TransformationMethod: LLM, DETERMINISTIC_RULE, LEXICAL_MATCH, TRANSLITERATION, API, STRUCTURED_FIELD, SOURCE_ASSERTED, HUMAN; TransformationCategory: EXTRACTION, TRANSLATION, GROUNDING, NORMALIZATION). The MeDIC model is itself in flux; align with it as it evolves. Lexical-match information comes from the computational alignment system, not a curated tag (D-021).

title: Semantic Alignment Provenance: Specific Methods / Specifications
explanation: The concrete, versioned workflow / rule set / specification, plus the named rules applied at each step with their own certainty (MeDIC applied_rules / PreprocessingRuleEnum). Makes questions such as 'which mappings were broadened by stripping a qualifier?' answerable by query.

title: Semantic Alignment Provenance: Execution Details
explanation: The ordered resolution chain (MeDIC model): each step records its input and output value, contiguous by construction (step n output = step n+1 input). For text sources: span anchoring (span role, character offsets, co-mentions). For relations: an assertion layer with trigger span + trigger cue (the verbatim words that establish the relation, checked against the source). Chains are kept intact inside the evidence item (D-061).

title: Semantic Alignment Provenance: Date
explanation: Timestamp per run, and per step where steps ran at different times (e.g. a cached translation reused from an earlier run). Together with the frozen mapping-set version it lets the revision process detect stale chains (D-061).

title: Semantic Alignment Provenance: Confidence Category
explanation: Per-step QUALITY CATEGORY describing what kind of match it was, rather than a generic HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW (MeDIC model): grounding curated / lexical_exact / lexical_exact_normalized / lexical_exact_surgery / source_asserted / unresolved; extraction verbatim / canonicalized / synonym / not_stated; normalisation curated / asserted_exact / deprecated_replacement / identity. Data-quality axis = SEPIO confidence; gates or flags lines, never evidence strength (D-062).

title: Semantic Alignment Provenance: Confidence Score
explanation: 0-1 confidence per step with a REQUIRED basis: MEASURED (a scorer evaluated this input), DETERMINISTIC (cannot be wrong, 1.0), PRIOR (assumed per-version constant, flagged as an assumption). Priors are pinned to the exact model or tool version, so an upgrade never silently inherits an old prior (MeDIC ConfidencePrior). Chain confidence = product of step confidences. Data quality = SEPIO confidence: gates or flags lines, never evidence strength (D-062).

title: Semantic Alignment Provenance: Human Review / Validation Status
explanation: Review of ALIGNMENT steps only ('did the machine read and link correctly?'); claim review is the assertion decision (EINT, D-045, D-053). Per-step status MACHINE / CANDIDATE / UNDER_REVIEW / CONFIRMED / REJECTED with reviewer and date. Curation decisions are inputs to the build, stored in versioned decision stores (e.g. SSSOM) that the build reads, never outputs that a rebuild would overwrite (MeDIC). The two reviews can diverge: grounding confirmed but claim rejected, or grounding rejected (line invalidated, D-052) but claim accepted on other evidence.

title: Evidence Interpretation Provenance: Agent
explanation: Human: ORCID, role and expertise/trust level as of the time of interpretation (D-049, D-051). AI: model + version, workflow/prompt version and agent trust level (D-050, D-052). A collective act is one interpretation with several participants, optionally attributed to a group agent, not N independent ones (D-046).

title: Evidence Interpretation Provenance: Method Types
explanation: Starting vocabulary of five method types: expert judgement (individual), consensus panel, LLM judgement, computed concordance (external assertion matched by SPO), rule-based strength assignment (per-claim-type rule, D-054). The type drives trust weighting (D-052) and enables audits such as 'claims resting only on computed concordance'.

title: Evidence Interpretation Provenance: Specific Methods / Specifications
explanation: Required for AI lines (workflow / prompt version, D-050) and rule-based lines (per-claim-type rule identifier + version, D-054). Optional for human lines (guideline / SOP followed, e.g. ClinGen lumping/splitting, Mondo mapping curation guide, maprule; D-051). A rule version change triggers recomputation and re-queueing of lines computed under the old version (D-048).

title: Evidence Interpretation Provenance: Date
explanation: Anchors the 'as of' semantics: a sign-off refers to the evidence packet as of time X (D-051); trust and quality levels are taken as of the interpretation date (D-049, D-060), so a later re-rating does not change an old line unless it is re-signed. Recency of an interpretation can inform the per-claim-type rules (D-054).

title: Evidence Interpretation Provenance: Context / Location
explanation: OPTIONAL field, not a hard requirement: the context of the interpretation act, i.e. the curation activity (GitHub issue / PR, curation call, panel meeting; D-036) and the interpreter's perspective / use context (D-051). Collective-act detection (D-046) is recorded on the act itself and does not depend on this field.

title: Assertion Provenance: Agent
explanation: Current (partial): curator ORCIDs on 31k axioms (curator responsible, D-004); ClinGen expert-panel affiliations and externally managed content providers (GARD, NORD) as asserters (D-002). Desired: the signer of the assertion decision that makes it a Mondo claim (D-048, D-053), with role and trust level as of signing; collective decisions recorded as one act with several participants (D-046). For automatic acceptance: the automated system acting under policy P plus the policy's human approver (D-064).

title: Assertion Provenance: Method Types
explanation: Routes by which a claim enters Mondo: (1) computed score + individual human sign-off (D-048); (2) computed score + consensus sign-off (D-046); (3) DELEGATED / POLICY-BASED automatic acceptance: a human authors and approves the decision procedure (thresholds, evidence types, channels, claim types) and an automated system applies it, to remove the bottleneck of thousands of clear synonyms and mappings (D-064); (4) provider authority for externally managed content, as one such policy (D-017); (5) BATCH SIGN-OFF on a curator-defined filter: the curator filters candidates (e.g. S >= 0.9 and supported by OMIM) and approves the result set at once, with banded review depth (none / eyeballed / spot-checked); the filter, frozen result set and review depth are recorded, and a no-look approval adds no evidence (D-066). Policies only auto-accept; rejection is always a human decision (D-053).

title: Assertion Provenance: Specific Methods / Specifications
explanation: Sign-off routes: the inclusion-score rule version (D-063, D-054) and the version of the evidence packet that was signed off (D-051). Delegated route: the policy identifier + version (D-064), which pins rule versions and thresholds. A policy or rule change triggers re-evaluation; claims that fall below a new threshold go to the human queue, never to automatic rejection.

title: Assertion Provenance: Date
explanation: Today essentially absent: term-level dc:date on 67 terms, 1 creation_date, per-axiom history only in git. Desired: the date of each assertion decision (sign-off or automatic acceptance under a policy, D-064). Claims are re-evaluated when rules, policies or evidence change, so a claim keeps a decision history, not only the latest date.

title: Assertion Provenance: Context / Location
explanation: Partial today: term tracker items on ~24,100 terms (which term was touched, not which axiom was decided) and ~720 axiom-level GitHub issue/PR sources mixed into the evidence slot (D-036). Desired: every assertion decision points to its context: change request (issue/PR), panel meeting or curation call for collective acts (D-046), or the automated run for policy-based acceptance (D-064), so a bad batch can be found and re-queued as a unit. On migration the axiom-level GitHub sources are recoded into this slot, not deleted.

title: Assertion Provenance: Confidence Category
explanation: A derived band of the computed inclusion score S (D-063), versioned with the rule, NOT a confidence asserted by the signer. A free-standing signer confidence would duplicate S, drift from it and bypass it without an audit trail. A signer who disagrees with S adds that knowledge as a new evidence line (D-050, D-053), so S moves for a recorded reason; this also settles the expertise override left open in D-063.

title: Assertion Provenance: Confidence Score
explanation: The score is the inclusion score S itself (D-063), recorded on each assertion decision with its scale (-1 to 1, sign = net support vs dispute), the rule version that computed it and, under a policy, the threshold it passed (D-064). Each re-evaluation adds a new S to the decision history. An AI agent's self-reported confidence is NOT this field: it is data quality on that agent's evidence line (D-062). Today only a handful of mondo-ai mappings carry LLM_confidence, which is evidence-level.

title: Encoding Provenance: Agent
explanation: Low priority for Mondo (D-065). Artifact level only (release file, statement-view dump), never per claim; today only the release versionIRI, the rest is reconstructable from git and the ODK image.

title: Encoding Provenance: Method Types
explanation: Low priority (D-065): artifact level only.

title: Encoding Provenance: Specific Methods / Specifications
explanation: The one encoding row that matters (D-065): Mondo's release encoding CHANGES MEANING. The export rules decide which xrefs become exactMatch, which are dropped, how preferredExternal direction (D-012) and value-set links (D-013) are rendered, and how statements are generated from the term-centric form (D-041, D-042). These meaning-changing transforms must be versioned and each release artifact must name the version it used, so 'why is this exactMatch' resolves to 'edit-file claim X, translated by rule set R vN'.

title: Encoding Provenance: Date
explanation: Low priority (D-065): artifact level, covered by the release versionIRI.

title: Encoding Provenance: System/Artifact
explanation: Low priority (D-065): artifact level only.

title: Encoding Provenance: Version
explanation: Low priority (D-065): the release version; per-claim versions are covered by the decision history (PROV.ASSERTION.DATE) and the signed packet version (D-051).

title: Retrieval Provenance: Agent
explanation: The pipeline (and version) that carried a claim over from an upstream resource, i.e. the agent of the 'copied from' origin (D-030): kBOOM merge (legacy; MONDO:Leader marker deleted, origin recoverable for ~57% of terms), mondo-ingest slurp and sync pipelines, externally managed content syncs (GARD, NORD; D-002, D-017), mondo-ai harvesting. Partly determines the proposing channel in the claim prior (D-063).

title: Retrieval Provenance: Source System
explanation: The upstream resource AND its release from which a claim was copied (origin, D-030) or against which a corroborating line was last checked (D-031). Today the resource is implied by the CURIE prefix or a MONDO:<SOURCE> tag (D-025); the release is never recorded.

title: Retrieval Provenance: Source System Role
explanation: Primary vs aggregator, because it drives independence in the inclusion score (D-063: one line per independence cluster). Aggregators in Mondo's sources: MedGen (largely from OMIM/Orphanet), EFO (rare diseases from Orphanet), UMLS, MalaCards. Recorded as a per-resource default (MedGen = aggregator), overridable where a resource is primary for some content. Builds on the provider vs asserter split (D-002).

title: Retrieval Provenance: Target System
explanation: No Mondo requirement (D-067): the target is constant (Mondo) for Mondo's own retrieval events, and downstream retrieval is the consumer's provenance to keep.

title: Retrieval Provenance: Target System Role
explanation: Not needed per claim, but releases should let consumers tell when Mondo is the primary source and when it passes on provider-managed content, so downstream independence counting is correct. Derivable from the assertion route (provider-authority policy, D-064), hence M (D-067).

title: Retrieval Provenance: Date
explanation: Two dates: when the claim or line was first attached (origin vs corroboration, D-030) and when it was last confirmed against a source release. Support lapses when a source drops a name or link (D-031), so the last-confirmed date is what lets stale support be detected and re-queued. Distinct from when the source itself produced the evidence (PROV.EI rows).

title: Retrieval Provenance: Original names/ids
explanation: Store the source identifier, the source's own label and the source release at attachment time. Lets label drift and repurposed or obsoleted source records trigger re-review (D-010), and keeps the mention text for machine-read evidence (MeDIC mention, PROV.SA rows). Today partial: mondo-ingest mapping sets carry source labels; the edit file carries only the ID.

title: C001 Term existence / obsoletion
explanation: Corroborating records are evidence; the record a term was copied from is provenance (D-030).

title: C002 Definition
explanation: Definition dbxrefs mean 'inspired by' (provenance, D-031); publications and web pages are the evidence.

title: C003 Synonym
explanation: Support is time-sensitive (D-031); lexical scores only as machine evidence lines.

title: C005 Negative subclass
explanation: External assertions of the positive subclass are evidence DISPUTING Mondo's claim (D-033).

title: C006 Mapping
explanation: Precision code gives the predicate, not evidence (D-006); scores from mondo-ai alignment.

title: C007 Disease attribute (definitional)
explanation: Expert-panel classifications (ClinGen) as guidelines; only definitional attributes (D-039).

title: C008 Subset membership
explanation: Mostly provider- or stakeholder-asserted (D-002).

title: C009 Metaclass (candidate)
explanation: A source's own typing, e.g. Orphanet group / disorder / subtype (D-040).

title: C010 Value-set membership (candidate)
explanation: e.g. OMIM included titles (D-013, D-040).
